prompt:
Style references only: the attached images set the painting style, the colours and the mood. Do not copy their content. Paint it as a concept artist's painted sketch sheet for a cozy, bright strategy game: loose hand-painted brushwork with visible strokes, soft painted light from a warm sunny afternoon coming from the front right, cheerful bright colours, a warm light cream paper background with a soft painted shadow under each object. It is a painting, not a 3D render, not low poly, not a game screenshot. Cozy and friendly like a storybook toy, never grim. No people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no letters, no watermark.

The sheet shows the rampart of a toy fortress built from chunky full-tile blocks on a board of square tiles of bright green grass, seen in a three-quarter view from well above, the way a board game is seen from a chair. Every block fills one whole square tile and stands about three quarters as tall as the tile is wide, so the rampart is a thick square-section wall with a flat stone walkway along its top and a grid of two by two square merlons, the teeth of a battlement, standing on each block's walkway. The stone is warm cream with crisp edges and narrow flat bevels, and blocks that share a side join into one continuous wall. One straight run of four blocks turns a corner and continues for three more blocks; the two blocks at the far end carry a second storey of the same block stacked on top, twice as tall, with merlons only on the upper storey. Below the run, smaller and alone on its own grass tile, stands one single block seen a little closer so its sides show. The look: the body of each block is set back a little on every side, so the wall is thinner in the middle and fatter at the top and at the foot. A low plinth as wide as the tile runs along the ground, and the walkway with its merlons overhangs the body on a row of small stone corbels, like a machicolated parapet, casting a deep shadow line under the overhang.
